questions.question: Match each trigonometric function to its definition in the context of a right-angled triangle
questions.explanation: Sine is defined as the ratio of the length of the opposite side to the hypotenuse, Cosine is the ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse, Tangent is the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side, and Secant is the ratio of the hypotenuse to the adjacent side.

questions.question: Put the steps to find the sine of an angle in a right-angled triangle in the correct order
items: Divide the length of the opposite side by the hypotenuse
questions.explanation: First, identify the opposite side and the hypotenuse, then divide the length of the opposite side by the hypotenuse, and finally write the result.

questions.question: Complete the sentence using the word bank: In a right-angled triangle, the $\sin(\theta)$ is equal to the ratio of the {{0}} side to the {{1}} side.
questions.template: In a right-angled triangle, the $\sin(\theta)$ is equal to the ratio of the {{0}} side to the {{1}} side.
questions.explanation: The sine of an angle in a right-angled triangle is defined as the ratio of the length of the side opposite the angle to the length of the hypotenuse.

questions.question: Mark each statement True or False: The unit circle is a circle with a radius of 1 centred at the origin of a coordinate plane.
statements: The unit circle is a circle with a radius of 1 centered at the origin of a coordinate plane.
The unit circle is a circle with a radius of 2 centered at the origin of a coordinate plane.
The unit circle is used to define trigonometric functions for all real numbers.
The unit circle is only used for acute angles.
questions.explanation: The unit circle is indeed a circle with a radius of 1 centred at the origin, and it is used to define trigonometric functions for all real numbers, not just acute angles.

questions.question: Tap the item that does NOT belong: Sine, Cosine, Tangent, Square Root
questions.explanation: Sine, Cosine, and Tangent are trigonometric functions, whereas Square Root is a mathematical operation.

questions.question:
Match each reduction formula to its description: I. $\sin(90^\circ - \theta) = \cos(\theta)$
II. $\cos(90^\circ - \theta) = \sin(\theta)$
III. $\tan(90^\circ - \theta) = \cot(\theta)$
IV. $\sec(90^\circ - \theta) = \csc(\theta)$
questions.explanation: Each pair correctly matches a reduction formula with its description based on complementary angles.

questions.question:
Put the steps to graph a sine function in the correct order: I. Identify the amplitude and period
II. Plot the key points
III. Draw the curve
IV. Label the axes
questions.explanation: First identify amplitude and period to set scale, then plot key points on labelled axes, then draw the smooth curve through them.

questions.question: Match each trigonometric function to its definition
questions.explanation: Sine is defined as the ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse, Cosine as the ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse, Tangent as the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side, and Secant as the reciprocal of Cosine.

questions.question: Put the steps to find the sine of an angle in a right triangle in the correct order
items: Identify the opposite side and the hypotenuse
Write the ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse
Calculate the sine value using a calculator
Label the sides of the triangle
questions.explanation: First, label the sides of the triangle, then identify the opposite side and the hypotenuse, next write the ratio, and finally calculate the sine value using a calculator.

questions.question: Complete the sentence using the word bank
questions.template: The sine of an angle in a right triangle is equal to the length of the {{0}} side divided by the length of the {{1}} side.
questions.explanation: The sine of an angle in a right triangle is defined as the ratio of the length of the opposite side to the length of the hypotenuse.
